data_quality_assurance:
During the project, data quality will be ensured through:
  • use of validated clinical assessment tools (e.g., MG-QOL, FSS),
  • adherence to standardized lab protocols (SOPs),
  • double data entry and verification,
  • statistical checks (e.g., range and consistency validation),
  • pseudonymisation and consistent coding.
After the project, data will:
  • remain available in RSU Dataverse with version control and DOI,
  • be updated if necessary with documented changes,
  • be overseen by the Principal Investigator as contact person for re-use or corrections,
  • be preserved long-term by RSU to ensure ongoing accessibility and reliability.
dataset.description: This dataset includes clinical evaluations, immune profiling, and viral load measurements from 100 Myasthenia Gravis (MG) patients and 65 healthy controls. The data were collected to investigate the relationship between immune system status, chronic viral infection (HHV-6A, HHV-6B, HHV-7), and fatigue in MG. The dataset supports biomarker discovery for disease progression prediction and fatigue management.

distribution.title:
The purpose of the data collection is to explore the interplay between immune dysregulation, chronic viral infection, and fatigue in patients with Myasthenia Gravis (MG). The data are collected to identify novel biomarkers—specifically immune and viral indicators—that can help predict the clinical course of MG and severity of fatigue. This aligns directly with the project’s objective to improve diagnostic and prognostic tools for MG, with an emphasis on fatigue as a critical symptom.
The dataset originates from a cohort of 100 MG patients and 65 healthy controls. Clinical data were collected using validated scales (MG Composite Score, MG-ADL, MG-QOL, and Fatigue Severity Scale). Biological samples (blood) were used for QuantiFERON Monitor immune function testing, cytokine profiling, and viral load detection for HHV-6A, HHV-6B, and HHV-7 via PCR/RT-PCR. The integration of clinical and molecular data supports the discovery of reliable biomarkers linked to MG progression and fatigue.

security_and_privacy.description:
Data security will be ensured before and during publication through the following measures:
  • Data will be stored on the RSU secure server (U: drive) with restricted access only for authorized team members.
  • Role-based access rights will be applied and updated as needed.
  • Raw data will be protected by RSU's firewall and accessible only within the RSU network.
  • Before publication, data will be pseudonymised, checked for quality, and reviewed to remove any personal identifiers.
  • Only final and verified datasets will be published in RSU Dataverse with appropriate documentation and licensing.

dataset.title: Patient data: Clinical, Immunological and Virological Data of Myasthenia Gravis Patients and Healthy Controls

dmp.description: This Data Management Plan (DMP) pertains to the research project focused on Myasthenia Gravis (MG), a rare autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. The project aims to identify novel biomarkers by investigating the interplay between immune dysregulation, systemic inflammation, and chronic viral infections (particularly HHV-6A, HHV-6B, and HHV-7). The ultimate goal is to develop tools for early prediction of disease progression and management of MG-related fatigue. The project involves clinical assessments, biological sample analysis, and molecular testing, including cytokine profiling and viral load quantification, carried out at Riga Stradins university and its affiliated centers.
dmp.ethical_issues_description:
The project involves the collection of personal and sensitive health data from human participants (Myasthenia Gravis patients and healthy controls), including clinical evaluations, questionnaire responses, and biological samples. Therefore, strict adherence to:
  • EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR),
  • Latvian national data protection laws,
  • and RSU Ethics Committee guidelines is required.
All participants will provide written informed consent. Personal identifiers will be stored separately from research data and will not be shared or published. Before publishing, all datasets will be pseudonymised, and only non-identifiable data will be made publicly available. No commercial or classified information is involved.

project.description: The project aims to identify new biomarkers of myasthenia gravis by studying the interactions between immune dysregulation, systemic inflammation, and chronic viral infection reactivation. By integrating in-depth analyses of cytokine profiles, immune system status, and viral activity (e.g., HHV-6/HHV-7), detect mechanisms that promote fatigue development and determine the course of the disease. The project aims to develop a scientific basis for biomarker-based tools that allow early prediction of the course of the disease and control the development of MG-related fatigue, significantly improving patient care.
project.title: Discovering Biomarkers in Myasthenia Gravis: Insights into Fatigue, Immune Dysregulation, and Viral Infections
